exposure: Intrapartum Cesarean Delivery Classification System (ICDCS) usage
indications for cesarean delivery (e.g., fetal, dystocia-inefficient uterine action, dystocia-efficient uterine action, persistent malposition, cephalopelvic disproportion)
outcome: patterns of subgroup indications for C-section
cohort: Women with single cephalic pregnancies at ≥37 weeks' gestation experiencing spontaneous or induced labor, observed over an 18-year period at an Irish tertiary maternity center and categorized into Robson groups 1, 2a, 3, 4a, 5a, and 5b.
finding: The Intrapartum Cesarean Delivery Classification System (ICDCS) was successfully used for 18 years, revealing consistent patterns of intrapartum cesarean delivery indications within and between Robson groups, providing a granular understanding of labor events and outcomes in conjunction with the Ten Group Classification System.
mod_finding: Over the 18-year period, there were significant increases in the overall cesarean delivery rate in Robson Groups 1 and 2a, increases in specific cesarean delivery indications, and an increase in the vaginal operative delivery rate, while oxytocin use decreased in Group 1.
